candidates.exact_span: As required by 40 CFR 127.16, all Discharge Monitoring Reports (DMRs) shall be electronically reported.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether DMRs must be electronically reported under 40 CFR 127.16 affects which monitoring submissions are obligatory for FY2025 and how missing or absent DMR evidence should be classified versus documented no-data or unresolved cases.

candidates.exact_span: identifies the receiving stream segment no, 20.6.4.401(San Juan River (Navajo Nation boundary at Hogback to Animas River) is impaired for turbidity sedimentation/siltation and E. coli bacteria.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Impairment for turbidity, sedimentation/siltation, and E. coli could affect which parameters have enforceable numeric limits and which monitoring requirements are treated as applicable, especially where limits are tied to TMDL or water-quality-driven obligations.

candidates.exact_span: The draft permit proposes E. coli limits consistently with the approved TMDL.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether E. coli limits are proposed consistently with the approved TMDL affects which enforceable numeric E. coli limit is treated as applicable for compliance comparison during FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The limitations and monitoring requirements set forth in the proposed draft are developed from the appropriate State WQS and are protective of those designated uses.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The stated basis that both numeric limitations and monitoring requirements derive from State WQS affects which limits are enforceable for compliance comparison and which monitoring obligations are considered permit-applicable rather than report-only or non-operative.

candidates.exact_span: interim or final effluent limitations must be as stringent as those in the previous permit, unless material and substantial alterations or additions to the permitted facility occurred after permit issuance which justify the application of a less stringent effluent limitation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The antibacksliding exception for less stringent limits after material and substantial facility changes affects whether revised draft limits or prior-permit limits govern FY2025 compliance comparisons when limit stringency differs.

candidates.exact_span: The proposed permit is slightly more restrictive than the previous permit since the Cyanide limits have been established in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishment of new Cyanide limits in the draft permit changes whether an enforceable numeric Cyanide limit exists and which limit value applies for FY2025 exceedance evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: the 30-day average TDS net incremental increase and loading limits have been revised downward to 449 mg/L (from 497 mg/L) and to 24,992 lbs/day (from 27,664 lbs/day), respectively, in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The revised TDS 30-day average net incremental increase and loading limit values directly determine the applicable numeric limits against which reported TDS measurements and loadings would be compared.

candidates.exact_span: For other pollutants (i.e., BOD5, TSS, pH, E. coli, and TRC), their limits are kept the same.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether BOD5, TSS, pH, E. coli, and TRC limits remain unchanged from the previous permit affects which numeric limit values are treated as applicable for FY2025 compliance comparisons versus newly revised draft values.
